_meta.caveats: General information, not legal advice. Clock usually starts at the first missed payment/last payment. Federal Reg F (12 CFR 1006.26) bars ALL third-party debt collectors from suing or threatening suit on time-barred debt nationwide; 'barred_extinguished' flags only extra STATE-law bars. 'revival' gives the general rule: in many states a payment only restarts a clock that is still running and cannot revive an already-expired debt. Several states limit their no-suit/no-revival rules to debt buyers (CT, NC, TX). Where courts have not settled which period applies to credit cards (IA, KS, UT), 'open' uses the LONGER period so users don't assume a debt is expired too early. Choice-of-law and borrowing statutes can shorten or lengthen the period. Federal student loans have no SOL. Time-barred debt can still appear on credit reports for 7 years. A suit on old debt must still be answered: the SOL is a defense the consumer must raise.

Alabama.note: Credit cards usually treated as open account (3 yrs). Payment restarts clock only before it expires.

Arizona.note: Credit cards 6 yrs by statute; other open accounts 3 yrs; written contracts signed out of state 4 yrs. Payment alone doesn't revive.

Arkansas.note: Open accounts without a signed writing: 3 yrs. Medical debt: 2 yrs from service or last payment.

California.note: Once expired, no one may sue or arbitrate (CCP 337(d)) and payment can't revive it. Payment/written ack restart only a running clock.

Colorado.note: 6 yrs for any liquidated debt, written or not.

Connecticut.note: Debt buyers can't sue on time-barred debt and a later payment doesn't revive it for them (P.A. 16-65).

Delaware.note: Signed acknowledgment of an unexpired debt gives 6 more yrs. Effect of a bare payment is unclear.

Florida.note: Only a signed writing revives expired debt. Hospital medical debt: 3 yrs from referral to collections.

Georgia.note: Credit cards can get 6 yrs if creditor produces the written card agreement (Hill v. Amex).

Idaho.note: Credit cards count as written (5 yrs); other unwritten accounts 4 yrs.

Illinois.note: Credit cards usually 5 yrs (unwritten) unless every key term is in a signed writing.

Iowa.note: Credit card period unsettled: 10 yrs or 5 yrs. Payment alone doesn't revive; needs signed writing.

Kansas.note: Credit card period unsettled: 5 or 3 yrs. Even a small payment can revive expired debt.

Kentucky.note: Written contracts signed before 7/15/2014: 15 yrs. Credit cards usually 5 yrs.

Louisiana.note: Loans (money lent), open accounts and credit cards: 3 yrs; promissory notes 5 yrs.

Maine.note: Collectors can't sue 6+ yrs after last activity; payment or acknowledgment doesn't revive (32 MRS 11013(8)).

Maryland.note: No consumer debt suit after SOL; payment or affirmation doesn't revive (CJP 5-1202).

Massachusetts.note: Pending bill would cut consumer debt to 5 yrs; not law as of check date.

Minnesota.note: Consumer debt: once expired, payment or reaffirmation doesn't revive it (Minn. Stat. 541.053).

Mississippi.note: Expired debt is extinguished. Payment/acknowledgment restarts only a still-running clock.

Missouri.note: Credit cards usually 5 yrs unless creditor shows an agreement you signed.

Montana.note: Written contracts were 8 yrs before 2023 amendments; older debts may differ.

Nebraska.note: Credit card classification unsettled (could be 5 yrs). Payment can revive expired debt.

Nevada.note: Since 2023 nothing revives expired debt and collection agencies can't sue on it. Hospital debt: disclosure required.

New Mexico.note: Even a small payment can revive expired debt; collectors must warn you first (AG rule 12.2.12).

New York.note: Consumer credit 3 yrs; nothing revives it once expired (CPLR 214-i). Medical debt 3 yrs from treatment.

North Carolina.note: Debt buyers can't sue or even try to collect time-barred debt (G.S. 58-70-115(4)).

Ohio.note: Consumer debt 6 yrs written or not; clock starts 30 days after last charge or payment.

Oregon.note: Collectors and debt buyers may not sue on time-barred debt (ORS 646.639). Interest charges don't restart the clock.

Rhode Island.note: No revival statute; common-law acknowledgment rules apply.

South Carolina.note: Even a small payment can revive expired debt.

Texas.note: Debt buyers can't sue on expired debt, and payment doesn't revive it (Fin. Code 392.307).

Utah.note: Credit card period unsettled: likely 6 yrs (2019 law), possibly 4.

Virginia.note: 3 yrs if you never signed the contract. Medical debt: 3 yrs from final invoice.

Washington.note: Licensed collectors can't sue on time-barred debt (RCW 19.16.250). Nothing revives an already-expired debt.

West Virginia.note: Only a signed written promise restarts the clock.

Wisconsin.note: Expired debt is extinguished (Wis. Stat. 893.05). Payment restarts only a still-running clock.

District of Columbia.note: Consumer debt (incl. medical) 3 yrs; suing on expired debt is illegal; payment doesn't revive it.

Puerto Rico.note: 4 yrs under 2020 Civil Code; debts before 11/28/2020 may be 15 yrs. Creditor demand letters can interrupt.
